spawn.facing: south-west, toward the table plaza (graffiti building on the left, fence and funbox on the right)
spawn.notes: LP2 34:38: the run opens on the start walkway with the plaza ahead, a graffitied building to the left, a fence and small ramp to the right and palms behind. PS12 says the tape becomes visible going straight down from the start, which makes it the first teaser (≈ 30 m away); this is not confirmed in LP2's small frames. Turning left drops into the pool within 2 s (LP2 34:39–34:41); from there the roof ring is 10 s away. Turning right leads along the fence to the north-west roofs (S, K).

guidance: The plaza and its two utility poles lie straight ahead of spawn; the cable is the plaza's only overhead line and the tape glows above it (PS12; LP2 35:07).
The pool beside the spawn walkway visibly backs onto low roofs, inviting the roof ring (LP2 34:39–34:48).
Letters on roof edges and rims read against the sky and the sea (E at the round roof's rim, LP2 34:49–34:51; T above the top roof's quarter pipe, LP2 35:02).
From the highest roof the whole plaza and the wire are framed below, and the roof edge points at the tape: the shrine's hint is to look around after the T.
Spray cans float above perimeter quarter pipes and teach where the VB transfer pairs are.
The magic bum relocates to the next spot after each ollie, so the goal itself guides the player around the level (PS12).
Heights are the only hazard seen: overshooting a roof drops the player to a lower layer (shrine warning at the E). LP2 shows no water or kill hazard; the beach is the outer boundary on VG.
designLogic: A two-way tape: the High Wire hangs between the plaza (tables) and the top roof, so the tape can be taken bottom-up (table → wire grind, the 1+2 guides' route) or top-down (drop from the highest roof, the LP2 route). One placement serves a short precise route and a long forgiving one.
The tape is the first teaser: on the main sightline from spawn, ≈ 30 m away (PS12), long before the player knows how to reach it. The roof ring around the plaza is the answer.
The roof ring is the level's spine: pool → low roof → round roof → cables → highest roof gathers one can, two letters and the tape in 31 s (LP2). The letters E and T mark it.
The pool next to spawn works as an elevator: three named exits (Wee Lil', Nice Mid Size, Siiiiiick Roof Gap) grade the same move by distance from the wall.

Graded thresholds on single objects recur: planters (two pops), the narrow quarter pipe (Up!/Up!!/And Away!!!), boarded tables (He Could Go.../All The Way.../Touchdown!!!), pool exits. One object yields several difficulty steps.

Cables are a navigation layer: radial cables on the round roof carry the player between roofs (LP2 34:55–34:58), and the tape sits on the plaza's cable. Wire grinds are introduced as connectors before the tape asks for one (1+2 route).
No unlocks at career position 5: after the Hangar's trigger-gated tape and School II's speed-gated roof, Venice's tape is in plain sight and is gated only by chaining roofs at speed.

Failure cost scales with height: plaza misses are cheap, but losing the roof ring costs ≈ 20–30 s, so the top-down route gives one attempt per climb. The plaza route (Ramp 2 Roof → Vent 2 Roof) is the designed way back up.
Goal objects teach the perimeter: spray cans on four perimeter vert spots and the pool; the bum's five spots cover the pit, the south-east, the north fence, the banner courtyard and spawn.
Cash rewards hard corners: three $250 icons sit at the plaza sculpture, the round roof and the south pit, and the 12 icons total $1,500 (VG; matches the shrine's '$500 + $1500').
Scores scale with the career: Pro 100,000 and Sick 200,000, against the Hangar's 25,000/75,000, assume the long roof lines and manual chains the layout offers.
Letter placement maps the two roof chains: E and T on the central/round roofs, S and K on the north-west roofs, A on the south-east terrace. Collecting S-K-A-T-E means touring every raised zone.
remakeChanges: Goals unchanged except for the added High Combo 20,000 (PS12).

Letters: PS12 (1+2) describes a single roof chain S → K → A → T → E (fence onto a building; K over a gap; grind the graffitied wall to the next roof for A; kicker to a roof with T over a quarter pipe; drop to the lower roof for E above a short ramp). In the original, A sits on the south-east terrace's curved rail (VG; LP2 36:13) and E on the round roof's rim (LP2 34:51). The remake appears to move A into the roof chain (inferred from text; not verified in LP12).

Tape: the 1+2 guides all describe the ground-up route. PS12: from a table, ollie up and grind the wire, which is precise. Thumbsticks: boost off the ramp, land, skate back to the second table on the left and ramp off it. Screenrant: max Speed, Air and Ollie stats help. LP2's original run uses the top-down roof drop instead. 1+2 keeps the top-down option: its street stat point is reached by ollieing off the end of the highest roof toward the wire.
Lighting: midday in the original (LP2) vs sunset in 1+2 (LP12 0:55–1:02), with denser graffiti. The wire still crosses the plaza's sky (LP12 0:55:38).
Gap list: PS12 adds On The Fence and Fence To Roof (not labelled on VG); VG's Huge Ramp 2 Roof is absent from PS12.

1+2 adds stat points (by the wire, on the roofs, above a banner rail and over a beach fence), the Vicarious Visions logo (up a wooden quarter pipe onto a wall, then a ramp) and the alien plushie (end of the wooden beach path).
transfer: High-wire crystal: string a rope or travelling rail from a roof edge down to a pole over a picnic plaza and hang the crystal ≈ 1 m above it near the high end. Bottom-up: from a ≈ 0.8 m table a full ollie peaks at ≈ 2.6 m, and the 2.1 m snap radius catches a wire up to ≈ 4.5 m, so drop the wire's low end to ≈ 4 m and let the grind carry up to the crystal. Top-down: the roof ring ends at an edge facing the crystal; ollie off through it.
Pool-as-elevator beside spawn: a bowl whose far wall transfers onto a low roof, with three graded exits (near, mid, far from the wall) that later serve as score gaps.

Roof ring with breadcrumbs: place 2–3 secondary pickups (crates or letters) on the ring before the crystal's launch roof (rim of a round roof, a rooftop quarter pipe) so the ring is learned before it is needed.
Visible tease: put the crystal on the spawn sightline ≈ 30 m away, above the plaza, so the level's first question is 'how do I get up there?'.
Moving pickup tour: a collectible that hops to the next of five fixed spots each time it is touched, leading the player through the districts in a fixed order.
Height-scaled failure: keep plaza retries cheap (table and wire within 3–5 s) and give the top-down route a designed lift back up (quarter pipe → roof → vent kicker) of ≈ 20 s.
openQuestions: The original A position: VG and LP2 put it on the south-east terrace rail, the shrine says 'a different roof, use the quarterpipe where all the tables are', and PS12 (1+2) puts it in the roof chain. Two editions or two readings of one spot?
Wire heights and the tape's exact height are estimates. Whether the original wire's low end is reachable from a table with stock stats is not shown (1+2 guides say it is precise and stat-dependent).
Original gap point values (only 1+2 values verified) and the points for VG's Huge Ramp 2 Roof.
Whether the bum's five spots and order are identical in the original (VG numbering matches PS12's order).
Which roof is the 'highest' in the shrine's T description: LP2 confirms the T over a quarter pipe on the roof facing the plaza; its height relative to the round roof is estimated only.
